Analysis: Issues in the xmdm= -gui Skill

=F0=9F=94=B4 Execution Engine Bug =E2=80=94 for_each is not implemented

The root cause of t= he add_new_record failure is in the execution engine, not= the skill logic itself. The error message we saw was:

Failed to execute 'querySelector': 'form[id$=3D"formNew"] tbody =
tr:nth-child(${fieldIndex + 1}) input' is not a valid selector.

The template ${fieldIndex + 1}= was never substit= uted =E2=80=94 it was passed literally as a CSS selector. This means= the engine does not support the for_each step= type at all. It appears to have fallen through and tried to execute the in= ner step as a raw template string.

This is an engine issue. The for_each construct needs to be implemented in the step executo= r.

=

=F0=9F=94=B4 Skill Bug =E2=80=94 add_new_record: Wrong parameter design for for_each

Even if for_each were implemented, there is a= logic error in the action:

"pa=
rameters": [{ "fieldValues": "object" }],
"for_each": "${fieldValues}",
"as": ["fieldIndex", "fieldValue"],
"fill": "...tr:nth-child(${fieldIndex + 1}) input"

The fieldValues parameter is k= eyed by field name= (e.g. {"Participant ID": "PART1", ...}= ), so when iterating, fieldIndex would be a string like <= code class=3D"rounded bg-muted px-1.5 py-0.5 font-mono text-sm" data-stream= down=3D"inline-code">"Participant ID", not a number. The expression = ${fieldIndex + 1} would produce "Participant ID1" =E2=80=94 an invalid selector.

Fix options:

=
  • Change= fieldValues to an array (ordered list of values), e.g. <= code class=3D"rounded bg-muted px-1.5 py-0.5 font-mono text-sm" data-stream= down=3D"inline-code">["PART1", "XEUR", ...], and iterate with a nume= ric index
  • OR kee= p the object keyed by field name, but resolve field names to row indices vi= a a lookup step rather than using the key directly as an index
<= h3 class=3D"mt-6 mb-2 font-semibold text-xl" data-streamdown=3D"heading-3">= =F0=9F=9F=A1 Skill Bug =E2=80=94 open_row_detail: Off-by-one indexing mismatch
"description": "Open the detail dialog for a specific row by its index",
"parameters": [{ "rowIndex": "number" }],
"click": "tbody tr:nth-child(${rowIndex}) button[title=3D\"Detail\"]"

The description says 0-based, but nth-child() is 1-based. Calling with rowIndex=3D0 produces nth-child(0) which matches nothing in CSS (we confi= rmed this live: it errored). Calling with rowIndex=3D= 1 returns the first row.

Either:

  • Change= the selector to nth-child(${rowIndex + 1}) an= d keep 0-based parameter (consistent with switch_tab_= by_text)
  • Or upd= ate the description to say 1-based
<= h3 class=3D"mt-6 mb-2 font-semibold text-xl" data-streamdown=3D"heading-3">= =F0=9F=9F=A1 Skill Bug =E2=80=94 add_new_record: Insufficient fill for PrimeFaces CellEditor

Even if the loop work= ed correctly, a plain fill step on the <input> is not sufficient for PrimeFaces CellEditor. The= server reads state from the .ui-cell-editor-output div,= not only the input value. During our live session, fields 0=E2=80=9310 wor= ked because the fill tool triggered PrimeFaces= events that updated the output div =E2=80=94 but field 11 (Date of Birth, = the last row) had an empty output div and was consistently rejected.

= The action needs an additional step to set the output div content:

=
document.querySelector('...tr:nth-child(N=
) .ui-cell-editor-output').textContent =3D value;

This is hard to express cleanly in the current declarative = step DSL =E2=80=94 it may require a script ste= p type in the engine, or a dedicated fill_cell_editor= step type.
